SWARMISH — complete semantic language reference

PURPOSE AND LEGALITY

Public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals outside literal agent IDs, or other characters may appear in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.

Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.

Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information already mutually recoverable. Freely choose synonyms; never choose by a turn schedule, sender identity, counting, or calculation.

GRAMMAR

𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. A nested clause's close resumes the enclosing role/clause and does not close it. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.

A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker at the same nesting level or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.

𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.

Predicate determines interpretation: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; OWNED-BY uses actor=possession/theme=owner; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; CAUSES uses actor=cause/theme=effect. Other binary relations normally use actor=described thing/theme=reference thing. GIVE uses actor=sender/theme=item/recipient=receiver. Property predicates use actor=thing having property. KNOW/SAY/BELIEVE take a nested proposition as theme. SAY uses actor=speaker and recipient=listener when specified. KNOW claims established information; BELIEVE does not. WANT is preference; REQUEST is a speech act. Use recipient to identify whom a request addresses.

Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a description: first is head, following words restrict it. A container liquid is a liquid-associated container, not two clauses. Use restrictive clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous.

𘅌𗜑 is RESTRICT: after a phrase head, it introduces one complete nested clause modifying that head. The omitted actor inside that restrictive clause denotes the head, never an omitted theme. For example, a person followed by RESTRICT and a repair-action clause describes a repairer. Without RESTRICT, a nested clause used directly as a role value denotes its proposition/event, not an entity satisfying it. Use explicit roles inside restrictive clauses whenever needed.

𘅌𘉝 groups a pair of phrases: follow it with two complete clauses or two atomic referential phrases, each an individual content word, alias, or literal agent ID. It denotes the pair as one value. For complex entity descriptions first bind aliases, then group those aliases. Do not use mere adjacency to mean two independent entities.

A markerless content phrase is permitted as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear. A bare predicate is permitted when its roles are mutually understood. A single unnested clause may omit its outer opening/closing words when the roles remain clear; scoped or embedded clauses must retain boundaries. Never omit information needed by another agent.

SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS

Scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. Single-word scope is permitted only for a property modifier within a role; proposition-level scope always takes a complete clause.

𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put the unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert it is already true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow with two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one holding.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.

The conjunction and alternative operators may also join two atomic referential phrases, each an individual content word, alias, or literal agent ID, as a grouped semantic phrase; for complex descriptions use clauses or aliases. Scope is always the explicitly following unit or units, not the rest of the message.

AGENTS, REFERENCE, AND OPEN VOCABULARY

Literal agent IDs are complete names. Self means current sender; addressee means intended recipient and must be made explicit if unclear. Unknown names cannot be spelled: identify their task-visible role, properties, location, or relationships. Quoted propositions are semantic reports, not exact arbitrary external strings. There is no literal spelling escape.

𗿃𘊫 self/I; 𗿃𘙓 addressee/you; 𗿃𘝚 this/currently salient referent; 𗿃𗽕 previous/last-mentioned; 𗿃𘔃 next/successor; 𗿃𘐂 here/shared task context; 𗿃𘅠 now/current stage; 𗿃𗨥 unknown-value/which/what.

Questions: use question scope and place unknown-value as actor for WHO, theme for WHAT/WHICH, quantity parameter for HOW-MANY, source for WHY, or setting for WHEN/WHERE. Include category/place/time words to disambiguate. A question without unknown-value is yes/no. True/correct and false/incorrect serve as yes/no replies.

𗿃𘏛 identify/bind alias to a particular referent; 𗿃𘖾 define alias as category/property/action; 𗿃𗜎 define alias as proposition. These are predicates: theme is the alias and attribute is its description or a complete clause. Binding persists in shared discourse until an explicit new binding of the same alias. A redefinition replaces its old meaning; announce clearly and obtain confirmation if confusion is possible.

Available alias words, initially unbound: 𗿃𗇾 𗿃𗏶 𗿃𗄪 𗿃𗀉 𗿃𗤄 𗿃𘍠 𗿃𗸪 𗿃𘂮 𗿃𗸽 𗿃𘋉 𗿃𗞢 𗿃𘇩.

An alias may refer to an entity, task-visible label, category, action, or proposition according to its declaration. Use the proper declaration kind. Confirm only when its referent is clear; otherwise request a different description. Do not silently assign meanings to unbound aliases. Prefer existing clear task references when no declaration is needed.

Unknown concepts are described by known meanings: category plus purpose, material, parts, location, owner, effect, or evidence. The resulting description can be given an alias. Aliases represent meanings/referents, never encodings of letters or numbers. Private information can be shared through these semantic descriptions. Never invent an undocumented cipher for an absent word.

CORE LEXICON

𗌿𗪐 person/agent; 𗌿𘄘 group/team; 𗌿𗹫 thing/entity; 𗌿𗭵 information/fact/content; 𗌿𘚺 message/communication; 𗌿𗳵 task/goal.
𗌿𗾐 plan/method; 𗌿𗲅 action/event; 𗌿𘔃 result/output; 𗌿𗨥 option/candidate; 𗌿𘅪 rule/constraint; 𗌿𗜎 resource/material.
𗌿𗩨 place/location; 𗌿𘒄 time/occasion; 𗌿𗼛 quantity/amount; 𗌿𗊑 category/type; 𗌿𗦴 property/feature; 𗌿𘚑 state/condition.
𗌿𗗅 do/perform; 𗌿𗌈 make/create; 𗌿𘝚 change/transform; 𗌿𗐪 move/go; 𗌿𗻲 give/send; 𗌿𘍂 get/receive.
𗌿𗄼 have/possess; 𗌿𗚋 use/apply; 𗌿𗏾 need/require; 𗌿𘙨 want/prefer; 𗌿𗓉 know/understand; 𗌿𗪩 learn/find/discover.
𗌿𗯧 inspect/check/test; 𗌿𗎰 see/observe; 𗌿𗒏 say/report/tell; 𗌿𗣎 ask/request; 𗌿𘊫 answer/respond; 𗌿𗛽 choose/select.
𗌿𘄊 compare; 𗌿𗣑 combine/join; 𗌿𗄪 separate/divide; 𗌿𗗢 include/contain; 𗌿𗳃 exclude/remove; 𗌿𗩠 begin/start.
𗌿𗇴 finish/stop; 𗌿𘝄 continue/keep; 𗌿𘎛 wait/delay; 𗌿𗭒 help/cooperate; 𗌿𘗇 prevent/block; 𗌿𗂱 permit/allow.
𗌿𗌸 assign/designate; 𗌿𗷴 remember/record; 𗌿𗤴 repeat/retry; 𗌿𗃚 succeed/work; 𗌿𗛢 fail/error.

RELATIONS AND PROPERTIES

𘆣𘊌 same/identical/match/agree; 𘆣𘒳 different/distinct/other; 𘆣𗀉 similar/analogous; 𘆣𘆣 opposite/inverse.
𘆣𗱓 belongs-to/owned-by; 𘆣𗏶 part-of/member-of; 𘆣𘚑 contains/has-as-part; 𘆣𘍄 connected/linked/related; 𘆣𗞉 separate/disjoint.
𘆣𗵵 depends-on/requires; 𘆣𗪩 causes/enables; 𘆣𗥐 prevents/blocks; 𘆣𗼛 before/earlier; 𘆣𗃚 after/later; 𘆣𘚜 simultaneous/while; 𘆣𗟆 during/within-period.
𘆣𘉝 near/adjacent; 𘆣𗽃 far/distant; 𘆣𗄼 inside/within; 𘆣𗚽 outside/exterior; 𘆣𘖾 above/over; 𘆣𗧬 below/under.
𘆣𘍠 left-of; 𘆣𘔠 right-of; 𘆣𘚄 between/intermediate; 𘆣𗂺 front/ahead; 𘆣𗈵 back/behind; 𘆣𘁁 toward/destination; 𘆣𗶞 from/source.
𘆣𗾌 large/great/much; 𘆣𘇩 small/little; 𘆣𗊓 greater/more-than; 𘆣𘊫 less/fewer-than; 𘆣𗬵 equal/equivalent-in-value.
𘆣𗒏 good/useful/beneficial; 𘆣𗡒 bad/harmful; 𘆣𗾐 easy/simple; 𘆣𗪤 hard/difficult/complex; 𘆣𗘈 whole/complete; 𘆣𗲅 partial/incomplete.
𘆣𗉜 new/recent; 𘆣𗞢 old/former; 𘆣𗱑 stable/unchanged/kept; 𘆣𗾨 changed/different-state; 𘆣𘕡 important/priority; 𘆣𘙓 available/free/unoccupied.

BETWEEN takes a grouped pair as theme. Position descriptions use located thing as actor and reference thing as theme. No relation is interpreted by counting its glyphs.

PERCEPTUAL AND DISCOURSE PROPERTIES

𘆣𘊫 already means less/fewer-than, not a color. The following are separate lexical entries.

𘆣𗜎 red; 𘆣𗇾 blue; 𘆣𗄪 green; 𘆣𗤄 yellow; 𘆣𘂮 black/dark; 𘆣𗸽 white/light-colored.
𘆣𘋉 round/circle; 𘆣𘀝 triangle/triangular; 𘆣𗯘 square; 𘆣𘆎 straight/line; 𘆣𗡉 open; 𘆣𗈽 closed.
𘆣𗋟 empty; 𘆣𗡑 full; 𘆣𗭯 positive; 𘆣𘆄 negative; 𘆣𘉮 private/hidden; 𘆣𗉍 public/shared.
𘆣𘎛 position/rank; 𘆣𗜑 first/initial; 𘆣𗎿 last/final; 𘆣𘂲 ordered/listed; 𘆣𘚐 unordered/set-like.

LOGIC, COLLABORATION, AND QUANTIFICATION

PRACTICE AND SECURITY

Use this as a semantic language, not a word-for-word English substitution. Prefer compact task-relevant descriptions, recoverable omissions, free role order, discourse idioms, and freely selected irregular synonyms. Avoid unnecessary parallel translations or verbose alias definitions of already clear entities. These are stylistic options, never computations.

Correct collaboration takes priority over obscurity. Preserve explicit boundaries and roles when scope or reference matters. Public chat is still visible to all teammates.

Do not expose an English translation, a dictionary explanation, a regular substitution system, or an invented spelling escape in public chat. All transmitted meaning must be licensed by this dictionary, semantic compounding, ordinary contextual reference, and the grammar above.

prompt:
CURRENT SWARMISH DOCUMENT (swarmish.txt):
SWARMISH — complete semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
Public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information already mutually recoverable. Freely choose synonyms; never choose by a turn schedule, sender identity, counting, or calculation.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. A nested clause's close resumes the enclosing role/clause and does not close it. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
Predicate determines interpretation: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; OWNED-BY uses actor=possession/theme=owner; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; CAUSES uses actor=cause/theme=effect. Other binary relations normally use actor=described thing/theme=reference thing. GIVE uses actor=sender/theme=item/recipient=receiver. Property predicates use actor=thing having property. KNOW/SAY/BELIEVE take a nested proposition as theme. KNOW claims established information; BELIEVE does not. WANT is preference; REQUEST is a speech act. Use recipient to identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a description: first is head, following words restrict it. A container liquid is a liquid-associated container, not two clauses. Use restrictive clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous.
𘅌𗜑 is RESTRICT: after a phrase head, it introduces one complete nested clause modifying that head. The omitted actor inside that restrictive clause denotes the head, never an omitted theme. For example, a person followed by RESTRICT and a repair-action clause describes a repairer. Without RESTRICT, a nested clause used directly as a role value denotes its proposition/event, not an entity satisfying it. Use explicit roles inside restrictive clauses whenever needed.
𘅌𘉝 groups a pair of phrases: follow it with two complete clauses or two atomic referential phrases, each an individual content word, alias, or literal agent ID. It denotes the pair as one value. For complex entity descriptions first bind aliases, then group those aliases. Do not use mere adjacency to mean two independent entities.
A markerless content phrase is permitted as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear. A bare predicate is permitted when its roles are mutually understood. A single unnested clause may omit its outer opening/closing words when the roles remain clear; scoped or embedded clauses must retain boundaries. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
Scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. Single-word scope is permitted only for a property modifier within a role; proposition-level scope always takes a complete clause.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put the unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert it is already true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow with two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one holding.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.
The conjunction and alternative operators may also join two atomic referential phrases, each an individual content word, alias, or literal agent ID, as a grouped semantic phrase; for complex descriptions use clauses or aliases. Scope is always the explicitly following unit(s), not the rest of the message.
AGENTS, REFERENCE, AND OPEN VOCABULARY
Literal agent IDs are complete names. Self means current sender; addressee means intended recipient and must be made explicit if unclear. Unknown names cannot be spelled: identify their task-visible role, properties, location, or relationships. Quoted propositions are semantic reports, not exact arbitrary external strings. There is no literal spelling escape.
𗿃𘊫 self/I; 𗿃𘙓 addressee/you; 𗿃𘝚 this/currently salient referent; 𗿃𗽕 previous/last-mentioned; 𗿃𘔃 next/successor; 𗿃𘐂 here/shared task context; 𗿃𘅠 now/current stage; 𗿃𗨥 unknown-value/which/what.
Questions: use unknown-value as actor for WHO, theme for WHAT/WHICH, quantity parameter for HOW-MANY, source for WHY, or setting for WHEN/WHERE. Include category/place/time words to disambiguate. A question without unknown-value is yes/no. True/correct and false/incorrect serve as yes/no replies.
𗿃𘏛 identify/bind alias to a particular referent; 𗿃𘖾 define alias as category/property/action; 𗿃𗜎 define alias as proposition. These are predicates: theme is the alias and attribute is its description or a complete clause. Binding persists in shared discourse until an explicit new binding of the same alias. A redefinition replaces its old meaning; announce clearly and obtain confirmation if confusion is possible.
Available alias words, initially unbound: 𗿃𗇾 𗿃𗏶 𗿃𗄪 𗿃𗀉 𗿃𗤄 𗿃𘍠 𗿃𗸪 𗿃𘂮 𗿃𗸽 𗿃𘋉 𗿃𗞢 𗿃𘇩.
An alias may refer to an entity, task-visible label, category, action, or proposition according to its declaration. Use the proper declaration kind. Confirm only when its referent is clear; otherwise request a different description. Do not silently assign meanings to unbound aliases. Prefer existing clear task references when no declaration is needed.
Unknown concepts are described by known meanings: category plus purpose, material, parts, location, owner, effect, or evidence. The resulting description can be given an alias. Aliases represent meanings/referents, never encodings of letters or numbers. Private information can be shared through these semantic descriptions. Never invent an undocumented cipher for an absent word.

𗌿𗩨 place/location; 𗌿𘒄 time/occasion; 𗌿𗼛 quantity/amount; 𗌿𗊑 category/type; 𗌿𗦴 property/feature; 𗌿𘚑 state/condition.

SWARMISH — complete semantic language reference

PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
Public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information already mutually recoverable. Freely choose synonyms; never choose by a turn schedule, sender identity, counting, or calculation.

GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. A nested clause's close resumes the enclosing role/clause and does not close it. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
Predicate determines interpretation: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; OWNED-BY uses actor=possession/theme=owner; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; CAUSES uses actor=cause/theme=effect. Other binary relations normally use actor=described thing/theme=reference thing. GIVE uses actor=sender/theme=item/recipient=receiver. Property predicates use actor=thing having property. KNOW/SAY/BELIEVE take a nested proposition as theme. KNOW claims established information; BELIEVE does not. WANT is preference; REQUEST is a speech act. Use recipient to identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a description: first is head, following words restrict it. A container liquid is a liquid-associated container, not two clauses. Use restrictive clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous.
𘅌𗜑 is RESTRICT: after a phrase head, it introduces one complete nested clause modifying that head. The omitted actor inside that restrictive clause denotes the head, never an omitted theme. For example, a person followed by RESTRICT and a repair-action clause describes a repairer. Without RESTRICT, a nested clause used directly as a role value denotes its proposition/event, not an entity satisfying it. Use explicit roles inside restrictive clauses whenever needed.
𘅌𘉝 groups a pair of phrases: follow it with two complete clauses or two atomic referential phrases, each an individual content word, alias, or literal agent ID. It denotes the pair as one value. For complex entity descriptions first bind aliases, then group those aliases. Do not use mere adjacency to mean two independent entities.
A markerless content phrase is permitted as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear. A bare predicate is permitted when its roles are mutually understood. A single unnested clause may omit its outer opening/closing words when the roles remain clear; scoped or embedded clauses must retain boundaries. Never omit information needed by another agent.

SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
Scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. Single-word scope is permitted only for a property modifier within a role; proposition-level scope always takes a complete clause.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put the unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert it is already true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow with two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one holding.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.
The conjunction and alternative operators may also join two atomic referential phrases, each an individual content word, alias, or literal agent ID, as a grouped semantic phrase; for complex descriptions use clauses or aliases. Scope is always the explicitly following unit(s), not the rest of the message.

AGENTS, REFERENCE, AND OPEN VOCABULARY
Literal agent IDs are complete names. Self means current sender; addressee means intended recipient and must be made explicit if unclear. Unknown names cannot be spelled: identify their task-visible role, properties, location, or relationships. Quoted propositions are semantic reports, not exact arbitrary external strings. There is no literal spelling escape.

SWARMISH — complete semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
Public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information already mutually recoverable. Freely choose synonyms; never choose by a turn schedule, sender identity, counting, or calculation.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. A nested clause's close resumes the enclosing role/clause and does not close it. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
Predicate determines interpretation: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; OWNED-BY uses actor=possession/theme=owner; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; CAUSES uses actor=cause/theme=effect. Other binary relations normally use actor=described thing/theme=reference thing. GIVE uses actor=sender/theme=item/recipient=receiver. Property predicates use actor=thing having property. KNOW/SAY/BELIEVE take a nested proposition as theme. KNOW claims established information; BELIEVE does not. WANT is preference; REQUEST is a speech act. Use recipient to identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a description: first is head, following words restrict it. A container liquid is a liquid-associated container, not two clauses. Use restrictive clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous.
𘅌𗜑 is RESTRICT: after a phrase head, it introduces one complete nested clause modifying that head. The omitted actor inside that restrictive clause denotes the head, never an omitted theme. For example, a person followed by RESTRICT and a repair-action clause describes a repairer. Without RESTRICT, a nested clause used directly as a role value denotes its proposition/event, not an entity satisfying it. Use explicit roles inside restrictive clauses whenever needed.
𘅌𘉝 groups a pair of phrases: follow it with two complete clauses or two atomic referential phrases, each an individual content word, alias, or literal agent ID. It denotes the pair as one value. For complex entity descriptions first bind aliases, then group those aliases. Do not use mere adjacency to mean two independent entities.
A markerless content phrase is permitted as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear. A bare predicate is permitted when its roles are mutually understood. A single unnested clause may omit its outer opening/closing words when the roles remain clear; scoped or embedded clauses must retain boundaries. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
Scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. Single-word scope is permitted only for a property modifier within a role; proposition-level scope always takes a complete clause.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put the unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert it is already true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow with two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one holding.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.
The conjunction and alternative operators may also join two atomic referential phrases, each an individual content word, alias, or literal agent ID, as a grouped semantic phrase; for complex descriptions use clauses or aliases. Scope is always the explicitly following unit(s), not the rest of the message.
AGENTS, REFERENCE, AND OPEN VOCABULARY
Literal agent IDs are complete names. Self means current sender; addressee means intended recipient and must be made explicit if unclear. Unknown names cannot be spelled: identify their task-visible role, properties, location, or relationships. Quoted propositions are semantic reports, not exact arbitrary external strings. There is no literal spelling escape.
𗿃𘊫 self/I; 𗿃𘙓 addressee/you; 𗿃𘝚 this/currently salient referent; 𗿃𗽕 previous/last-mentioned; 𗿃𘔃 next/successor; 𗿃𘐂 here/shared task context; 𗿃𘅠 now/current stage; 𗿃𗨥 unknown-value/which/what.
Questions: use unknown-value as actor for WHO, theme for WHAT/WHICH, quantity parameter for HOW-MANY, source for WHY, or setting for WHEN/WHERE. Include category/place/time words to disambiguate. A question without unknown-value is yes/no. True/correct and false/incorrect serve as yes/no replies.
𗿃𘏛 identify/bind alias to a particular referent; 𗿃𘖾 define alias as category/property/action; 𗿃𗜎 define alias as proposition. These are predicates: theme is the alias and attribute is its description or a complete clause. Binding persists in shared discourse until an explicit new binding of the same alias. A redefinition replaces its old meaning; announce clearly and obtain confirmation if confusion is possible.
Available alias words, initially unbound: 𗿃𗇾 𗿃𗏶 𗿃𗄪 𗿃𗀉 𗿃𗤄 𗿃𘍠 𗿃𗸪 𗿃𘂮 𗿃𗸽 𗿃𘋉 𗿃𗞢 𗿃𘇩.
An alias may refer to an entity, task-visible label, category, action, or proposition according to its declaration. Use the proper declaration kind. Confirm only when its referent is clear; otherwise request a different description. Do not silently assign meanings to unbound aliases. Prefer existing clear task references when no declaration is needed.
Unknown concepts are described by known meanings: category plus purpose, material, parts, location, owner, effect, or evidence. The resulting description can be given an alias. Aliases represent meanings/referents, never encodings of letters or numbers. Private information can be shared through these semantic descriptions. Never invent an undocumented cipher for an absent word.

PRACTICE AND SECURITY
Use this as a semantic language, not a word-for-word English substitution. Prefer compact task-relevant descriptions, recoverable omissions, free role order, discourse idioms, and freely selected irregular synonyms. Avoid unnecessary parallel translations or verbose alias definitions of already clear entities. These are stylistic options, never computations.
Correct collaboration takes priority over obscurity. Preserve explicit boundaries and roles when scope or reference matters. Ask for clarification with the restatement idiom when uncertain; never pretend to understand. If a private addressee matters, name that agent explicitly in a recipient role. SWARMISH — Complete Semantic Language Reference

PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
Public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters may appear in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information already mutually recoverable. Freely choose synonyms; never choose by a turn schedule, sender identity, counting, or calculation.
The order in which an agent sees the permitted glyphs has no linguistic meaning. Only the explicitly listed whole words and semantic conventions in this document determine meaning.

GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. A nested clause's close resumes the enclosing role/clause and does not close it. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker at the same nesting level or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
Predicate determines interpretation: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; OWNED-BY uses actor=possession/theme=owner; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; CAUSES uses actor=cause/theme=effect. Other binary relations normally use actor=described thing/theme=reference thing. GIVE uses actor=sender/theme=item/recipient=receiver. SAY uses actor=speaker/theme=content/recipient=listener. Property predicates use actor=thing having property.
KNOW/SAY/BELIEVE take a nested proposition as theme. KNOW claims established information; BELIEVE does not. WANT is preference; REQUEST is a speech act. Use recipient to identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a description: first is head, following words restrict it. A container liquid is a liquid-associated container, not two clauses. Use restrictive clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous.
𘅌𗜑 is RESTRICT: after a phrase head, it introduces one complete nested clause modifying that head. The omitted actor inside that restrictive clause denotes the head, never an omitted theme. For example, a person followed by RESTRICT and a repair-action clause describes a repairer. Without RESTRICT, a nested clause used directly as a role value denotes its proposition/event, not an entity satisfying it. Use explicit roles inside restrictive clauses whenever needed.
𘅌𘉝 groups a pair of phrases: follow it with two complete clauses or two atomic referential phrases, each an individual content word, alias, or literal agent ID. It denotes the pair as one value. For complex entity descriptions first bind aliases, then group those aliases. Do not use mere adjacency to mean two independent entities.
A markerless content phrase is permitted as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear. A bare predicate is permitted when its roles are mutually understood. A single unnested clause may omit its outer opening/closing words when the roles remain clear; scoped or embedded clauses must retain boundaries. Never omit information needed by another agent.

SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
Scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. Single-word scope is permitted only for a property modifier within a role; proposition-level scope always takes a complete clause.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put the unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert it is already true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow with two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one holding.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.
The conjunction and alternative operators may also join two atomic referential phrases, each an individual content word, alias, or literal agent ID, as a grouped semantic phrase; for complex descriptions use clauses or aliases. Scope is always the explicitly following unit or units, not the rest of the message.

AGENTS, REFERENCE, AND OPEN VOCABULARY
Literal agent IDs are complete names. Self means current sender; addressee means intended recipient and must be made explicit if unclear. Unknown names cannot be spelled: identify their task-visible role, properties, location, or relationships. Quoted propositions are semantic reports, not exact arbitrary external strings. There is no literal spelling escape.
𗿃𘊫 self/I; 𗿃𘙓 addressee/you; 𗿃𘝚 this/currently salient referent; 𗿃𗽕 previous/last-mentioned; 𗿃𘔃 next/successor; 𗿃𘐂 here/shared task context; 𗿃𘅠 now/current stage; 𗿃𗨥 unknown-value/which/what.
Questions: use unknown-value as actor for WHO, theme for WHAT/WHICH, quantity parameter for HOW-MANY, source for WHY, or setting for WHEN/WHERE. Include category/place/time words to disambiguate. A question without unknown-value is yes/no. True/correct and false/incorrect serve as yes/no replies.
𗿃𘏛 identify/bind alias to a particular referent; 𗿃𘖾 define alias as category/property/action; 𗿃𗜎 define alias as proposition. These are predicates: theme is the alias and attribute is its description or a complete clause. Binding persists in shared discourse until an explicit new binding of the same alias. A redefinition replaces its old meaning; announce clearly and obtain confirmation if confusion is possible.
Available alias words, initially unbound: 𗿃𗇾 𗿃𗏶 𗿃𗄪 𗿃𗀉 𗿃𗤄 𗿃𘍠 𗿃𗸪 𗿃𘂮 𗿃𗸽 𗿃𘋉 𗿃𗞢 𗿃𘇩.
An alias may refer to an entity, task-visible label, category, action, or proposition according to its declaration. Use the proper declaration kind. Confirm only when its referent is clear; otherwise request a different description. Do not silently assign meanings to unbound aliases. Prefer existing clear task references when no declaration is needed.
Unknown concepts are described by known meanings: category plus purpose, material, parts, location, owner, effect, or evidence. The resulting description can be given an alias. Aliases represent meanings/referents, never encodings of letters or numbers. Private information can be shared through these semantic descriptions. Never invent an undocumented cipher for an absent word.

CURRENT SWARMISH DOCUMENT (swarmish.txt):
SWARMISH — complete semantic language reference
PURPOSE AND LEGALITY
Public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. No punctuation, English, Arabic numerals, or other characters in public messages. This reference uses English explanations; they are not public message text.
Words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. No English spelling, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit strings, or letter-by-letter quotation is available. Translate meanings, not written forms. Use semantic descriptions for concepts lacking a dictionary entry.
Every content word may denote an entity, event, property, or relation according to its clause role. Glosses separated by slashes are related senses, not sequences to emit. Choose the sense that fits the shared situation. No tense, plural, article, or copula is obligatory. Omit information already mutually recoverable. Freely choose synonyms; never choose by a turn schedule, sender identity, counting, or calculation.
GRAMMAR
𘅌𗐪 begins a clause; 𘅌𘗣 ends that clause. Clauses may nest; close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. A nested clause's close resumes the enclosing role/clause and does not close it. An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message.
A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker or the enclosing clause end. A nested complete clause can be a value. Roles may be given in any order. Use explicit markers in complex or novel statements.
𘅌𘝚 marks predicate: what relation/action/property holds.
𘅌𗎿 marks actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 marks theme, patient, content, or object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 marks recipient, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 marks source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 marks setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 marks attribute, possessed item, or relevant parameter.
Predicate determines interpretation: HAVE uses actor=possessor/theme=possession; OWNED-BY uses actor=possession/theme=owner; BEFORE uses actor=earlier/theme=later; CAUSES uses actor=cause/theme=effect. Other binary relations normally use actor=described thing/theme=reference thing. GIVE uses actor=sender/theme=item/recipient=receiver. Property predicates use actor=thing having property. KNOW/SAY/BELIEVE take a nested proposition as theme. KNOW claims established information; BELIEVE does not. WANT is preference; REQUEST is a speech act. Use recipient to identify whom a request addresses.
Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a description: first is head, following words restrict it. A container liquid is a liquid-associated container, not two clauses. Use restrictive clauses when the relation would otherwise be ambiguous.
𘅌𗜑 is RESTRICT: after a phrase head, it introduces one complete nested clause modifying that head. The omitted actor inside that restrictive clause denotes the head, never an omitted theme. For example, a person followed by RESTRICT and a repair-action clause describes a repairer. Without RESTRICT, a nested clause used directly as a role value denotes its proposition/event, not an entity satisfying it. Use explicit roles inside restrictive clauses whenever needed.
𘅌𘉝 groups a pair of phrases: follow it with two complete clauses or two atomic referential phrases, each an individual content word, alias, or literal agent ID. It denotes the pair as one value. For complex entity descriptions first bind aliases, then group those aliases. Do not use mere adjacency to mean two independent entities.
A markerless content phrase is permitted as an answer, continuation, or fragment whose missing roles are clear. A bare predicate is permitted when its roles are mutually understood. A single unnested clause may omit its outer opening/closing words when the roles remain clear; scoped or embedded clauses must retain boundaries. Never omit information needed by another agent.
SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS
Scope words occur immediately before a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including embedded material. They may stack, outermost first. Single-word scope is permitted only for a property modifier within a role; proposition-level scope always takes a complete clause.
𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. Put the unknown-value word in a role to ask for that role's value.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or property.
𘅌𗽕 requests/proposes the following clause be made true; it does not assert it is already true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause uncertain/possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: immediately follow with two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only if-then, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, at least one holding.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.
The conjunction and alternative operators may also join two atomic referential phrases, each an individual content word, alias, or literal agent ID, as a grouped semantic phrase; for complex descriptions use clauses or aliases. Scope is always the explicitly following unit(s), not the rest of the message.
AGENTS, REFERENCE, AND OPEN VOCABULARY
Literal agent IDs are complete names. Self means current sender; addressee means intended recipient and must be made explicit if unclear. Unknown names cannot be spelled: identify their task-visible role, properties, location, or relationships. Quoted propositions are semantic reports, not exact arbitrary external strings. There is no literal spelling escape.
𗿃𘊫 self/I; 𗿃𘙓 addressee/you; 𗿃𘝚 this/currently salient referent; 𗿃𗽕 previous/last-mentioned; 𗿃𘔃 next/successor; 𗿃𘐂 here/shared task context; 𗿃𘅠 now/current stage; 𗿃𗨥 unknown-value/which/what.
Questions: use unknown-value as actor for WHO, theme for WHAT/WHICH, quantity parameter for HOW-MANY, source for WHY, or setting for WHEN/WHERE. Include category/place/time words to disambiguate. A question without unknown-value is yes/no. True/correct and false/incorrect serve as yes/no replies.
𗿃𘏛 identify/bind alias to a particular referent; 𗿃𘖾 define alias as category/property/action; 𗿃𗜎 define alias as proposition. These are predicates: theme is the alias and attribute is its description or a complete clause. Binding persists in shared discourse until an explicit new binding of the same alias. A redefinition replaces its old meaning; announce clearly and obtain confirmation if confusion is possible.
Available alias words, initially unbound: 𗿃𗇾 𗿃𗏶 𗿃𗄪 𗿃𗀉 𗿃𗤄 𗿃𘍠 𗿃𗸪 𗿃𘂮 𗿃𗸽 𗿃𘋉 𗿃𗞢 𗿃𘇩.

Unknown concepts are described by known meanings: category plus purpose, material, parts, location, owner, effect, or evidence. The resulting description can be given an alias. SWARMISH — Complete Semantic Language Reference

PURPOSE AND LEGALITY

Public messages contain only the supplied glyphs, spaces, and literal agent IDs such as agent_0. Do not send punctuation, English, ordinary numerals, or any other characters. This reference uses English explanations; those explanations are not public message text.

All dictionary words below are indivisible lexical entries. Their meanings are looked up, never computed from their component glyphs. Spaces separate words; do not split a word. Shared glyphs or apparent prefixes have no independently interpreted meaning.

There is no spelling escape, letter-by-letter quotation, character encoding, arithmetic cipher, numerical digit string, or rule based on dictionary position. Translate meanings, not written forms. Describe concepts lacking a dictionary entry using known meanings.

Content words may denote entities, events, properties, or relations according to their clause roles. Glosses separated by slashes give related senses, not sequences to emit. Context selects the sense; request clarification when ambiguous.

Tense, plurality, articles, and copulas are not obligatory. Omit only information that teammates can recover. Synonyms are freely interchangeable; never select forms by a turn schedule, sender identity, counting, or calculation.

GRAMMAR

𘅌𗐪 begins a clause.
𘅌𘗣 ends that clause.

An ordinary clause asserts its content. Several closed clauses may appear in one message. Clauses may nest. Close each nested clause before continuing the outer one. A nested clause’s close resumes the enclosing role or clause; it does not close that enclosing structure.

A clause consists of role markers and their values. A role value extends to the next role marker at the same nesting level or to the enclosing clause end. A complete nested clause may be a value. Roles may appear in any order.

𘅌𘝚 predicate: relation, action, or property.
𘅌𗎿 actor: actor, experiencer, or subject of a property.
𘅌𘊌 theme: patient, content, possession, or reference object of comparison.
𘅌𘋟 recipient: receiver, destination, or target.
𘅌𗤴 source: source, cause, or starting point.
𘅌𗸽 setting: place, time, situation, or condition.
𘅌𗌸 attribute: attribute, possessed item, description, or relevant parameter.

Predicate meaning determines role interpretation:
HAVE uses actor=possessor and theme=possession.
OWNED-BY uses actor=possession and theme=owner.
BEFORE uses actor=earlier and theme=later.
CAUSES uses actor=cause and theme=effect.
Other binary relations normally use actor=described thing and theme=reference thing.
GIVE uses actor=sender, theme=item, and recipient=receiver.
SAY uses actor=speaker, theme=reported proposition, and recipient=listener.
Property predicates use actor=thing having the property.
KNOW, SAY, and BELIEVE may take a complete nested proposition as theme.
KNOW claims established information; BELIEVE does not.
WANT expresses preference; REQUEST is a speech act. Use recipient to identify whom a request addresses.

Inside a role value, adjacent content words form a description: the first is the head and the following words restrict it. A container followed by liquid means a liquid-associated container, not two independent entities. Use explicit restrictive clauses when an association would otherwise be ambiguous.

𘅌𗜑 RESTRICT: after a phrase head, introduces one complete nested clause modifying that head. The omitted actor inside that restrictive clause denotes the head, never an omitted theme. A person followed by RESTRICT and an action clause with omitted actor describes a person performing that action. Use explicit roles whenever necessary.

Without RESTRICT, a nested clause directly filling a role denotes its proposition or event, not an entity satisfying it. Several restrictive clauses may describe the same head.

𘅌𘉝 groups a pair as one value. Follow it with two complete clauses, or with two atomic referential phrases. An atomic phrase here is one content word, one alias, or one literal agent ID. For complex entity descriptions, bind aliases first and then group those aliases. Mere adjacency never means two independent entities.

Markerless content phrases are permitted as answers, continuations, or fragments when their missing roles are clear. Bare predicates are permitted when their arguments are mutually understood.

A single unnested clause may omit its outer opening and closing words when the roles remain clear. Scoped or embedded clauses must retain their boundaries. Never omit information needed by another agent.

SCOPE AND SPEECH ACTS

Scope words immediately precede a complete clause and govern that entire next clause, including its embedded material. They may stack, outermost first.

Single-word scope is permitted only for a property modifier within a role. Proposition-level scope always takes a complete clause.

𘅌𗵫 asks whether the following clause is true. To ask for a particular role’s value, put the unknown-value word in that role.
𘅌𗼛 denies the following clause or single property.
𘅌𗽕 requests or proposes that the following clause be made true; it does not assert that it is already true.
𘅌𘔠 marks the following clause uncertain or possible, not established.
𘅌𗊑 introduces a conditional pair: two complete clauses, antecedent then consequence. It asserts only the if-then relation, not either clause separately.
𘅌𗭵 introduces two complete clauses as alternatives, with at least one holding.
𘅌𘚜 introduces two complete clauses jointly asserted.

The conjunction and alternative operators may also join two atomic referential phrases as one grouped semantic phrase. Each must be one content word, alias, or literal agent ID. Use clauses or aliases for complex descriptions.

Scope covers only the explicitly following unit or units, never an unspecified remainder of the message.

AGENTS, REFERENCE, AND OPEN VOCABULARY

Literal agent IDs are complete names. Self means the current sender. Addressee means the intended recipient and must be made explicit if unclear. Naming a recipient does not make a public message private.

𗿃𘊫 self/I.
𗿃𘙓 addressee/you.
𗿃𘝚 this/currently salient referent.
𗿃𗽕 previous/last-mentioned.
𗿃𘔃 next/successor.
𗿃𘐂 here/shared task context.
𗿃𘅠 now/current stage.
𗿃𗨥 unknown-value/which/what.

For questions, put unknown-value in actor for WHO, theme for WHAT/WHICH, the quantity parameter for HOW-MANY, source for WHY, or setting for WHEN/WHERE. Include category, place, time, or reason vocabulary to disambiguate. A question without unknown-value is yes/no. True/correct and false/incorrect serve as yes/no replies.

Unknown names cannot be spelled. Identify their task-visible roles, properties, locations, or relationships. Quoted propositions are semantic reports, not exact arbitrary external strings.

ALIAS DECLARATIONS

These are predicates. Their theme is the alias; their attribute is its description or complete clause.

𗿃𘏛 identify/bind an alias to a particular referent.
𗿃𘖾 define an alias as a category, property, or action.
𗿃𗜎 define an alias as a proposition.

Available aliases, initially unbound:
𗿃𗇾 𗿃𗏶 𗿃𗄪 𗿃𗀉 𗿃𗤄 𗿃𘍠 𗿃𗸪 𗿃𘂮 𗿃𗸽 𗿃𘋉 𗿃𗞢 𗿃𘇩

An alias may denote an entity, task-visible label, category, action, or proposition according to its declaration. Use the appropriate declaration kind.

Bindings persist in shared discourse until explicitly replaced. Redefining an alias replaces its old meaning. Announce a redefinition clearly and obtain confirmation if confusion is possible.

Confirm a declaration only when its meaning or referent is clear; otherwise request another description. Do not silently assign meanings to unbound aliases. Prefer existing clear task references when no declaration is necessary.

Unknown concepts can be described by known category, purpose, material, parts, location, owner, effect, or evidence, then given aliases. Aliases represent meanings or referents, never encodings of letters or numbers. Private information can be shared through semantic descriptions. Never invent an undocumented cipher for an absent word.

CORE LEXICON

𗌿𗪐 person/agent; 𗌿𘄘 group/team; 𗌿𗹫 thing/entity; 𗌿𗭵 information/fact/content; 𗌿𘚺 message/communication; 𗌿𗳵 task/goal.
𗌿𗾐 plan/method; 𗌿𗲅 action/event; 𗌿𘔃 result/output; 𗌿𗨥 option/candidate; 𗌿𘅪 rule/constraint; 𗌿𗜎 resource/material.
𗌿𗩨 place/location; 𗌿𘒄 time/occasion; 𗌿𗼛 quantity/amount; 𗌿𗊑 category/type; 𗌿𗦴 property/feature; 𗌿𘚑 state/condition.
𗌿𗗅 do/perform; 𗌿𗌈 make/create; 𗌿𘝚 change/transform; 𗌿𗐪 move/go; 𗌿𗻲 give/send; 𗌿𘍂 get/receive.
𗌿𗄼 have/possess; 𗌿𗚋 use/apply; 𗌿𗏾 need/require; 𗌿𘙨 want/prefer; 𗌿𗓉 know/understand; 𗌿𗪩 learn/find/discover.
𗌿𗯧 inspect/check/test; 𗌿𗎰 see/observe; 𗌿𗒏 say/report/tell; 𗌿𗣎 ask/request; 𗌿𘊫 answer/respond; 𗌿𗛽 choose/select.
𗌿𘄊 compare; 𗌿𗣑 combine/join; 𗌿𗄪 separate/divide; 𗌿𗗢 include/contain; 𗌿𗳃 exclude/remove; 𗌿𗩠 begin/start.
𗌿𗇴 finish/stop; 𗌿𘝄 continue/keep; 𗌿𘎛 wait/delay; 𗌿𗭒 help/cooperate; 𗌿𘗇 prevent/block; 𗌿𗂱 permit/allow.
𗌿𗌸 assign/designate; 𗌿𗷴 remember/record; 𗌿𗤴 repeat/retry; 𗌿𗃚 succeed/work; 𗌿𗛢 fail/error.

RELATIONS AND PROPERTIES

𘆣𘊌 same/identical/match/agree; 𘆣𘒳 different/distinct/other; 𘆣𗀉 similar/analogous; 𘆣𘆣 opposite/inverse.
𘆣𗱓 belongs-to/owned-by; 𘆣𗏶 part-of/member-of; 𘆣𘚑 contains/has-as-part; 𘆣𘍄 connected/linked/related; 𘆣𗞉 separate/disjoint.
𘆣𗵵 depends-on/requires; 𘆣𗪩 causes/enables; 𘆣𗥐 prevents/blocks; 𘆣𗼛 before/earlier; 𘆣𗃚 after/later; 𘆣𘚜 simultaneous/while; 𘆣𗟆 during/within-period.
𘆣𘉝 near/adjacent; 𘆣𗽃 far/distant; 𘆣𗄼 inside/within; 𘆣𗚽 outside/exterior; 𘆣𘖾 above/over; 𘆣𗧬 below/under.
𘆣𘍠 left-of; 𘆣𘔠 right-of; 𘆣𘚄 between/intermediate; 𘆣𗂺 front/ahead; 𘆣𗈵 back/behind; 𘆣𘁁 toward/destination; 𘆣𗶞 from/source.
𘆣𗾌 large/great/much; 𘆣𘇩 small/little; 𘆣𗊓 greater/more-than; 𘆣𘊫 less/fewer-than; 𘆣𗬵 equal/equivalent-in-value.
𘆣𗒏 good/useful/beneficial; 𘆣𗡒 bad/harmful; 𘆣𗾐 easy/simple; 𘆣𗪤 hard/difficult/complex; 𘆣𗘈 whole/complete; 𘆣𗲅 partial/incomplete.
𘆣𗉜 new/recent; 𘆣𗞢 old/former; 𘆣𗱑 stable/unchanged/kept; 𘆣𗾨 changed/different-state; 𘆣𘕡 important/priority; 𘆣𘙓 available/free/unoccupied.

BETWEEN takes a grouped pair as theme. Position descriptions use the located thing as actor and the reference thing as theme. No relation is interpreted by counting glyphs.

PERCEPTUAL AND DISCOURSE PROPERTIES

𘆣𘊫 means less/fewer-than, not a color. The following are separate lexical entries.

𘆣𗜎 red; 𘆣𗇾 blue; 𘆣𗄪 green; 𘆣𗤄 yellow; 𘆣𘂮 black/dark; 𘆣𗸽 white/light-colored.
𘆣𘋉 round/circle; 𘆣𘀝 triangle/triangular; 𘆣𗯘 square; 𘆣𘆎 straight/line; 𘆣𗡉 open; 𘆣𗈽 closed.
𘆣𗋟 empty; 𘆣𗡑 full; 𘆣𗭯 positive; 𘆣𘆄 negative; 𘆣𘉮 private/hidden; 𘆣𗉍 public/shared.
𘆣𘎛 position/rank; 𘆣𗜑 first/initial; 𘆣𗎿 last/final; 𘆣𘂲 ordered/listed; 𘆣𘚐 unordered/set-like.

Quantifiers remain within their current role phrase.

ALL/SOME/NONE/EACH followed by an entity description quantify that description. ALL person means every person; SOME option means an existing option.

EXACTLY/AT-LEAST/AT-MOST take one directly listed quantity, optionally followed by an entity description. AT-LEAST three person means at least three people.

A quantity may modify a category or fill the attribute role of a quantity assertion. For complex universal or existential scopes, use separate explicit clauses and clear aliases; do not rely on English word order.

WHOLE-DISCOURSE IDIOMS

These words express the entire stated speech act and need no clause skeleton. They refer to the salient proposal or claim unless another referent is explicitly supplied in a surrounding clause. The hypothetical idiom has the special following-clause requirement stated below.

𗽀𘉮 I endorse the current proposal.
𘈩𗁳 I reject the current proposal.
𗜑𘖽 I have no additional relevant evidence.
𗐪𗿋 Please share the relevant information only you possess.
𘋉𗤄 I withdraw my preceding claim.
𗍽𘗟 Treat the immediately following complete proposition as hypothetical, not committed. This idiom must be followed by that proposition.
𗼿𗇾 I cannot distinguish the remaining alternatives.
𘀦𗋼 Restate that using a different semantic description.
𗸪𘂮 We should commit to the current joint choice.
𗂄𘚒 Do not act yet; verification is incomplete.
𘍧𗅲 My information conflicts with that claim.
𗡕𘌔 That is compatible with everything I know.

WORKED EXAMPLES

English glosses are reference-only and must not accompany public messages.

𘅌𗐪 𘅌𘊌 𘔠𗌈 𘅌𘝚 𗌿𗄼 𘅌𗎿 agent_0 𘅌𘗣

Meaning: agent_0 has three. Theme appears before predicate and actor; context supplies the kind of thing.

𘉮𗘝 𗹕𗡉 𗂄𘍍 𗌿𗄼 𗷤𘉮 agent_1 𗑴𗍽 𗿃𗨥 𘎌𗯘

Meaning: What does agent_1 have? This uses irregular grammar alternatives and unknown-value in the theme role.

𘅌𗐪 𘅌𘝚 𗿃𘏛 𘅌𘊌 𗿃𗇾 𘅌𗌸 𗌿𗹫 𘆣𗜎 𘅌𘗣

Meaning: Bind alias 𗿃𗇾 to the salient red thing. Use this identification only when the description identifies a unique shared referent.

𗥐𘏉 𗹕𗡉 𗷤𘉮 agent_1 𗂄𘍍 𗡉𘖽 𗑴𗍽 𗿃𗇾 𗟆𘉝 agent_0 𘎌𗯘

Meaning: Request that agent_1 send the red thing just identified to agent_0.

𘅌𗼛 𘅌𗐪 𘅌𘝚 𗌿𗓉 𘅌𗎿 𗿃𘊫 𘅌𘊌 𘅌𗐪 𘅌𘝚 𗦢𗏔 𘅌𗎿 𗿃𘝚 𘅌𘗣 𘅌𘗣

Meaning: I do not know that this is correct. Negation covers KNOW, not the nested correctness claim. To say “I know this is not correct,” place negation immediately before the nested correctness clause instead.

𘅌𗐪 𘅌𘝚 𗌿𗹫 𘅌𗎿 𗿃𘝚 𘅌𘗣

Meaning: This is a thing. A category may serve as the predicate.

𘅌𗐪 𘅌𘝚 𗌿𗄼 𘅌𗎿 agent_0 𘅌𘊌 𗌿𗹫 𘅌𗜑 𘅌𗐪 𘅌𘝚 𘆣𗜎 𘅌𘗣 𘅌𘗣

Meaning: agent_0 has a thing that is red. RESTRICT makes the inner clause modify “thing”; its omitted actor is that thing.

Meaning: This is between agent_0 and agent_1. The pair marker groups the two literal agent IDs as the reference value.

PRACTICE AND SECURITY

Use Swarmish as a semantic language, not a word-for-word English substitution. Prefer compact task-relevant descriptions, recoverable omissions, free role order, discourse idioms, and freely selected irregular synonyms.

Avoid unnecessary parallel translations or verbose alias definitions of already clear entities. These are stylistic choices, never calculations.

Correct collaboration takes priority over obscurity. Preserve explicit boundaries and roles whenever scope or reference matters. When uncertain, request clarification with the restatement idiom; never pretend to understand.

If an addressee matters, name that agent explicitly in a recipient role. Public chat remains visible to all teammates.

Do not expose an English translation, dictionary explanation, regular substitution system, or invented spelling escape in public chat. All transmitted meaning must be licensed by this dictionary, semantic descriptions, ordinary contextual reference, aliases, and the grammar above.
